newsitem.title: NORWAY: Norway North Sea output disrupted at weekend.
newsitem.headline: Norway North Sea output disrupted at weekend.

text.p: Norway's Saga Petroleum ASA said on Sunday that crude production remained halted at the North Sea oilfields Tordis and Vigdis but that Snorre's output was back to normal at the weekend.
Spokeswoman Karin Oevsteboe said output at the 82,000 barrels per day (bpd) Tordis field was shut in as planned on Friday because of burgeoning storage capacity at the Gullfaks C platform.
"We are waiting for Gullfaks to start normal loadings again," she told Reuters.
Oddjan Lange, a spokesman for Gullfaks operator Statoil, or Den norske stats oljeselskap AS, said the field was running at minimum production but that the weather outlook for Monday looked fine.
"It looks like we can load tomorrow at Gullfaks," he said.
North Sea loadings by shuttle tankers have been disrupted recently because of hurricanes.
Tordis is tied back to Gullfaks C while Snorre pumps crude to Statfjord A for final processing, storage and loading on to shuttle tankers.
Saga on Saturday went back to normal production at the 230,000 bpd Snorre oilfield after a tanker began loading crude at the Statfjord development.
"Statfjord is at full production," Lange said. "Storage capacity is fine until Monday morning. But we must see loading at Statfjord on Monday to keep up full production."
The 30,000 bpd Vigdis field, which pumps oil to Snorre for processing before being piped to Gullfaks A for shipping, was shut down late on Thursday with gas compressor problems.
"We are still waiting for the delivery of equipment. We will know more tomorrow," Oevsteboe said.
